season.evidence: Stored Jul-Sep; Boston Basin condition reports and Mountaineers say the approach gully is half snow in early July and loose scree late, and the basin is an excellent late-season destination; log histogram peaks Jun-Aug.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Complete Aug 13 round trip, summited, but no logged route and a blank report; the peak has three routes, one far easier, so I cannot say it is the 5.10- face.
Logged SE Ridge; report describes the arete pitch and rappels.
Easy climbing with straightforward pitches and good protection; the standard ridge route, not the 5.10- face.
Easy climb to the summit after a snow chute approach.

facts.text: In July the bottom of the approach gully is guarded by a moat, and a short wall of snow must be climbed to reach the chute.
In mid-July a steep snowfield above the gully runs out badly; consider a couple of pickets or a belay, and the gully exit in crampons can feel close to fifth class.
Several parties have climbed the wrong gully; compare your gully with a photo overlay before committing.
In July the last rappel down the gully wall is about 30 m and lands at a moat, so a doubled 60 m rope helps clear it.

notes: No track names or describes the Southeast Face. The reports describe the ridge route and share the approach; the SE Ridge route (already has tracks) is the right owner of these tracks. The facts apply to the shared approach and descent.
